A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SDF-1 is a potent activator of Akt-dependent survival pathways in neurons.
CXCR4 is an antiapoptotic coreceptor in neuronal and glial cells, and that HIV-1 gp120(II-B) and SDF1alpha have different intrinsic efficacies to activate CXCR4-mediated survival pathways.
CXCR4 is a "promiscuous" receptor, with the potential to elicit both beneficial and detrimental responses in the brain, depending on the cellular context.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the outcome of the interaction of CXCR4 with gp120 and SDF- 1 alpha is pathway dependent and that the intrinsic efficacy (i.e., the efficiency with which CXCR4 is activated) of these ligands may be significantly different.
